title: What is known about 1RB0RC_0LA0RA_0LD0RA_1LE---_0LF1LB_1LA1LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_0LA0RA_0LD0RA_1LE---_0LF1LB_1LA1LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At a left turn the tape is 0 1 x1 1 x2 1 …: a sea of 01 in which some 0s (the defects xi = 1) are 1s. The rightward sweep complements every defect bit (pair 01 to 10, 11 to 00); the leftward sweep carries the word 110110 across the sea, 12 steps a pair, and the defects it meets change it. A round trip is thus a finite-state transducer on the defect string, a step of a cellular-automaton-like rule; the defects form triangles and drift. Both sweep rules over the sea are proved in Lean.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (10,000 by the kernel alone); the C simulator finds none in 10<sup>9</sup>.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,711 cells have been visited and 22,323 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: The sweeps over the sea, for every length and any tape around: A> (01)^n becomes (10)^n A> and a defect pair 11 becomes 00 (rightward, 2 steps a pair); (10)^n A> 110110 becomes A> 110110 (10)^n (leftward, the head carries 110110, 12 steps a pair), and the same seen from state F.

claims.title: A step of a cellular-automaton-like rule
claims.text: At every left turn the cells of one parity are all 1 and the others carry the defect bits; the whole tape changes from one round trip to the next (no frozen part). The defect string is not an XOR (linear) function of a window of the previous one: the best such fit with up to 3 neighbours fails on 13% of cells.

claims.title: Sibling
claims.text: 1RB1RD_1LC0LC_0RD0LB_1RF0LE_0RD---_0RA1RC runs the same mechanism with the roles of the sweeps exchanged (its leftward sweep is the plain one, its rightward sweep carries 0110); the two runs are not the same up to renaming.

claims.title: The halt needs 1 C>0 or 1 F>1
claims.text: The only halting transition D1 is reached only from 1 C>0 or 1 F>1. In the first 109 steps C reads a 0 71,429,798 times and F reads a 1 71,421,176 times, never with a 1 on the left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The defect dynamics is a deterministic rule on bit strings, but neither linear nor obviously simple; a proof would need the full transducer of the leftward sweep (it has a few states: the carried word changes at defects) and an invariant of the defect strings that excludes the halting patterns.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 49,711 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,711 cells (30,100 left of the start, 6,300 right), with a density of 1s of 0.449.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A sea with defects
html: At a left turn the tape is 0 1 x1 1 x2 1 …: a sea of 01 pairs, the 0s of some pairs replaced by 1s (defects). In the picture below each row is the tape at a left turn and a cell is black where two neighbouring cells are equal, that is, at the defects; the regular sea is grey.

Each round trip maps the defect string to a new one: the rightward sweep complements it, the leftward sweep rewrites it with a small finite memory. It is one step of a cellular-automaton-like rule, applied to a string that gets a few cells longer each time.

sections.heading: A question about the defect rule
html: The machine halts from 1 C>0 or 1 F>1 (D then reads a 1). Each happens about 71 million times in the first 109 steps, always with a 0 on the left. Those moments are inside the leftward sweep’s handling of defects, so a halt would be a particular defect configuration. No invariant of the defect strings that rules it out is known.

summary: A sea of 01 pairs carrying a string of defects; each round trip is a finite-state transducer on the defect string, like one step of a cellular automaton, and the defects form Sierpinski-like triangles.

sections.heading: How it works
paragraphs: The tape is a sea of the word 01, with defects: at a left turn the tape reads 0 1 x1 1 x2 1 x3 …, every second cell a 1, the others 0 except at defects. The rightward sweep is the simplest possible: it turns every pair 01 into 10 and every 11 into 00, complementing the defect bits. The leftward sweep is a zigzag that carries the word 110110 leftward 2 cells per 12 steps; when it meets a defect the carried word changes for a while and the new defects are written.

So each round trip applies a finite-state transducer to the string of defect bits, like one time step of a one-dimensional cellular automaton. Drawn turn after turn, the defects form triangles and diagonal streaks, a structure reminiscent of additive automata but not linear. Whether the halting pattern can ever be produced is a question about this rule.
